name: Fish sauce (fermented anchovy/marine sauce)

Pb.label: read-across from EU 2023/915 muscle meat of fish Pb 300 — fish sauce is a marine (fish-derived) product; the fish-muscle lead ML is the source-appropriate sovereign value.

Cd.source_scope: fish in general, except sardine, eel, and swordfish
Cd.label: read-across from Costa Rica RTCR 409 'fish in general' Cd 50 — the strictest sovereign fish-muscle cadmium ML.

tAs.label: read-across from AU-NZ Standard 1.4.1 fish tAs 2000 — total arsenic in fish is high but predominantly organic; the tighter inorganic control is the operative arsenic ceiling.

iAs.source_scope: muscle meat of fish, species other than those listed under Annex I 3.4.5.2
iAs.label: read-across from EU 2025/1891 muscle meat of fish inorganic-arsenic 100 — the toxic-species control; strictly below the total-arsenic read-across, so both are published.

tHg.source_scope: listed lower-mercury fish and cephalopods/marine gastropods, including cod, herring, mackerel, salmon/trout species listed, sardine/pilchard, sole, whiting, and others
tHg.label: read-across from EU 2023/915 lower-mercury fish tHg 300 — fish sauce is made from small forage fish (anchovy), which fall in the lower-mercury tier.

MeHg.label: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). The MeHg value (500 ug/kg) is not below the binding total mercury ceiling (300 ug/kg), so methylmercury is governed by and bounded by the total mercury ceiling; no separate MeHg ceiling is published. It is enforced by reflex speciation whenever tHg is elevated.

Ni.rationale: No sovereign nickel ML exists for fish sauce and fish are not nickel accumulators (the EU nickel regulation sets no fish ML). No concentration pathway comparable to a soybean or a hydrogenated fat operates. Rebuttable and audited each build.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign total-chromium ML exists for fish sauce; the only food chromium MLs in the register are dairy. Rebuttable and audited each build.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS screen; reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel number for a food; it is the reflex-speciation species. Any total-chromium exceedance is speciated, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: IC-ICP-MS Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Sn.rationale: Tin migrates only from tinplate cans; fish sauce is sold in glass or plastic, not tinplate. No non-canned tin pathway exists.

Al.rationale: No sovereign aluminium ML exists for fish sauce and no aluminium pathway operates. Rebuttable and audited each build.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; face value, no reconstitution; read-across / control / not-material for unregulated cells; no occurrence percentiles)
lineage_note: No sovereign sets a fish-sauce ML. Fish sauce is a fermented marine product (anchovy hydrolysate), so every metal reads across from the fish-muscle sovereign MLs of the marine source: Pb 300 (EU muscle meat of fish), Cd 50 (Costa Rica fish in general), tAs 2000 (AU-NZ fish), iAs 100 (EU 2025/1891 muscle meat of fish), tHg 300 (EU lower-mercury fish). The generic Vietnam 'Sauce' MLs (tHg 50 etc.) are deliberately NOT applied: fish sauce is a marine fermentate whose contaminant profile follows its fish source, not the condiment-sauce category — and Vietnam, the world's largest fish-sauce producer, does not cap nuoc mam mercury at the generic-sauce 50 (anchovy-based fish sauce routinely exceeds it), which confirms nuoc mam sits outside that category. The generic-sauce values are retained in the audit trail as a different product form. Methylmercury IS material here — the aquatic methylation pathway is the whole point of a marine read-across — and is read across from the fish MeHg ML (Mexico NOM-242 500); it is then reconciled against total mercury, and because 500 is not below the 300 total-mercury ceiling it is subsumed (bounded by tHg, enforced by reflex speciation). Inorganic arsenic (100) is published alongside total arsenic (2000) because it is a strictly tighter toxic-species control: arsenic in fish is high but predominantly organic (arsenobetaine).

warnings: fish-sauce[default].tAs: informational — stricter rows exist for a different product form (SG 1000 [tomato ketchup and other sauces]; VN 1000 [Sauce])
fish-sauce[default].tHg: informational — stricter rows exist for a different product form (VN 50 [Sauce])
